arrayConsistency.swapAndPopVerdict: CONSISTENT. USDE preserved at index 1 throughout. Every array member has isRegisteredStrategy==true and a non-zero strategyTokens entry; both removed strategies have isRegisteredStrategy==false and strategyTokens==0. No duplicate, no dangling pointer, no USDE collateral damage. addYieldStrategy reverts StrategyAlreadyRegistered on dup and removeYieldStrategy reverts StrategyNotRegistered on absent (idempotency guards in script make both no-ops on re-run).

residualBalanceCheck.purpose: Does removeYieldStrategy strand un-skimmed surplus belonging to live SYA clients in the OLD strategies at retirement?
residualBalanceCheck.verdict: NO STRANDED VALUE. 2.2 fully drains both OLD strategies (staker via migrateOut, minter via totalWithdrawal, accumulator surplus via skimSurplus->owner) BEFORE 2.3 retires them. At the moment of removeYieldStrategy both clients read zero on both balance and principal. removeYieldStrategy only mutates SYA bookkeeping; it never touches the strategy's funds, so even hypothetical residual would remain recoverable by the owner via the strategy's own emergencyWithdraw/withdrawAsOwner (and DecommissionOldStrategies sweeps it). No SYA NAV corruption: the strategy is simply no longer iterated by claim()/getTotalYield().

unintendedEffectsNote: No state write, event, or external mutation beyond the 4 intended SYA registry mutations (2 adds + 2 removes) and their 4 events. The USDe market strategy registration is preserved untouched. mainnet-addresses.ts is not touched (no JS chain). No ownership change, no token transfer, no approval, no pause-state change.

idempotency.result: Second run is a CLEAN NO-OP (all 4 isRegisteredStrategy guards short-circuit add/remove), array length stays 3, _verify() passes both times. No half-rewired stuck state observed for the happy path.

clusterChecks.DecommissionOldStrategies: ys-swap-lineage script (story 065 step 8); makes OLD strategies inert (emergencyWithdraw residual -> owner, deauthorize clients, revoke withdrawers, pause). Touches the OLD strategies' OWN config, NOT the SYA registry. Not in the saga-2 npm flow. No double-retire conflict with 2.3 (different surface: SYA registry vs strategy ACL/pause). If both ran, order-independent — 2.3 deregisters from SYA; Decommission kills the strategy contract. No stranded-value hazard because 2.2 already drains the strategies to zero before either retires them.
clusterChecks.doubleRunVerdict: 2.3's removeYieldStrategy is the authoritative saga-2 SYA-deregistration. The two ys-swap siblings are an alternative (superseded) route and are not part of saga-2; they would not be double-run as part of this flow. Residual hazard: DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA's hardcoded dead SYA (0x3bBE) is a latent footgun if an operator confuses routes — out of 2.3's scope but noted.
